claims.text: Adding approximately 2–3 at.% Al to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
A 2–3 at.% Al addition will promote in situ formation of a continuous, slow-growing Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will be thin and adherent.
Al added to the alloy will segregate to the surface during high-temperature exposure.
Surface-enriched Al will oxidize preferentially to form a continuous alumina scale.
The alumina scale has sufficiently low oxygen diffusivity to act as a barrier to oxygen transport.
The alumina diffusion barrier will slow further oxidation and pesting of the underlying alloy.
The 2–3 at.% Al addition will largely preserve room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical properties.
Relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-modified alloy will exhibit reduced oxidation penetration after a 5 h exposure to air at 800–1000 °C.
Relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-modified alloy will exhibit reduced oxide-scale spallation after a 5 h exposure to air at 800–1000 °C.
The Al-modified alloy will retain yield strength and tensile ductility within a useful range for high-temperature applications.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance under comparable high-temperature conditions.
The proposed intervention is applicable in air at 800–1000 °C for exposure times around 5 h.
The effects of 2–3 at.% Al on phase stability and microstructural evolution in equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr are not fully known.
It is uncertain whether 2–3 at.% Al is sufficient to form protective alumina without degrading mechanical properties.
